subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, trust, and failure semantics should that API use?
rationale: The remaining work defines a public plugin/security boundary around persisted config mutation, so automation should not choose the hook contract or failure semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design the API first
options.body: Define a documented config-write hook contract covering all config mutation paths, with explicit ordering, typed reject results, actor metadata, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep built-in guards only
options.body: Close or defer the plugin veto and rely on schema validation, SecretRef preflight, base-hash writes, and the agent config-write allowlist instead.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower interception point only for agent-issued `config.patch` and `config.apply`, accepting that other config writers will not be covered.

recommendation.title: Design the API first
recommendation.body: Define a documented config-write hook contract covering all config mutation paths, with explicit ordering, typed reject results, actor metadata, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the clearest issue-thread product/security review and have the strongest observed history on gateway config mutation safeguards.
